summary.short: Treasury rule (31 CFR part 850), effective 2 January 2025, requiring U.S. persons to notify Treasury of, or barring them from, investments in Chinese, Hong Kong or Macau entities active in semiconductors, quantum technologies and AI, according to technology-specific criteria and compute thresholds.
summary.long: Part 850 implements Executive Order 14105 under IEEPA. It covers U.S. persons' acquisitions of equity or contingent equity, equity-like loans, conversions, greenfield and brownfield projects, joint ventures and limited-partner stakes in non-U.S. funds involving a 'covered foreign person': a person of a country of concern (as listed in the Order's Annex) engaged in a covered activity, or a person that derives more than 50% of its revenue, net income, capital expenditure or operating expenses from such persons. Prohibited transactions involve EDA software, front-end, advanced-packaging and EUV equipment, advanced chip design and fabrication (non-planar or 16/14 nm logic, 128-layer NAND, 18 nm DRAM), advanced packaging, supercomputers, quantum computers and components, military or surveillance AI, AI trained with more than 10^25 operations (10^24 using primarily biological sequence data), and listed entities. Other chip activities and AI for military, cyber or robotic uses, or trained with more than 10^23 operations, are notifiable within 30 days. Exceptions cover publicly traded securities, registered funds, LP commitments of $2 million or less, buyouts of country-of-concern interests and pre-2025 binding commitments; Treasury may grant national interest exemptions. Violations carry IEEPA civil penalties (greater of $250,000, inflation-adjusted, or twice the transaction value), criminal penalties and divestment orders.

territorial_scope.description: Binds U.S. persons (including foreign branches of U.S. entities and, through reasonable-steps and notification duties, their controlled foreign entities) with respect to investments in or involving persons of a country of concern, wherever the joint venture or asset is located.

evidence.quote: The term U.S. person means any United States citizen, lawful permanent resident, entity organized under the laws of the United States or any jurisdiction within the United States, including any foreign branch of any such entity, or any person in the United States.

thresholds.value_text: greater than 10^23 computational operations (e.g., integer or floating-point operations)
thresholds.measurement: Total operations used to train the AI system; Treasury to assess the criterion periodically and update it through public notice (Note 1 to § 850.217)
thresholds.consequence: A covered transaction with a person developing such an AI system is a notifiable transaction (if not prohibited)
thresholds.conditions: AI system not described in § 850.224(j) or (k); covered foreign person or joint venture develops it; fine-tuning strictly for internal non-commercial use does not by itself trigger (Note 3)

evidence.quote: Trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^23 computational operations (e.g., integer or floating-point operations).

thresholds.value_text: greater than 10^25 computational operations (e.g., integer or floating-point operations)
thresholds.measurement: Total operations used to train the AI system; Treasury to assess the criterion periodically and update it through public notice (Note 1 to § 850.224)
thresholds.consequence: A covered transaction with a person developing such an AI system is a prohibited transaction
thresholds.conditions: Covered foreign person or joint venture develops the AI system; fine-tuning strictly for internal non-commercial use does not by itself trigger (Note 3)

evidence.quote: Develops any AI system that is trained using a quantity of computing power greater than: (1) 10^25 computational operations (e.g., integer or floating-point operations)

thresholds.consequence: A covered transaction with a person developing such an AI system is a prohibited transaction
thresholds.conditions: Training data primarily biological sequence data

evidence.quote: 10^24 computational operations (e.g., integer or floating-point operations) using primarily biological sequence data

thresholds.variable_text: performance parameters in Export Control Classification Number 3A090.a
thresholds.value_text: meets or exceeds the performance parameters in Export Control Classification Number 3A090.a in supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR part 774
thresholds.measurement: Parameters as set in the Export Administration Regulations Commerce Control List (moves with any EAR amendment)
thresholds.consequence: A covered transaction with a person designing such integrated circuits is a prohibited transaction; design of other ICs is notifiable (§ 850.217(a))

evidence.quote: Designs any integrated circuit that meets or exceeds the performance parameters in Export Control Classification Number 3A090.a in supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR part 774

thresholds.consequence: Designing (§ 850.224(c)) or fabricating (§ 850.224(d)(6)) such integrated circuits makes the covered transaction prohibited

thresholds.value_text: a production technology node of 16/14 nanometers or less

evidence.quote: Logic integrated circuits using a non-planar transistor architecture or with a production technology node of 16/14 nanometers or less, including fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) integrated circuits

thresholds.measurement: Layer count of NAND memory ICs
thresholds.consequence: Fabricating such NAND memory integrated circuits makes the covered transaction prohibited

evidence.quote: NOT-AND (NAND) memory integrated circuits with 128 layers or more

thresholds.measurement: Technology node of DRAM ICs measured as half-pitch
thresholds.consequence: Fabricating such DRAM integrated circuits makes the covered transaction prohibited

evidence.quote: Dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) integrated circuits using a technology node of 18 nanometer half-pitch or less

thresholds.consequence: Developing, installing, selling or producing such a supercomputer makes the covered transaction prohibited

thresholds.value_text: more than 50 percent of its revenue
thresholds.measurement: Annual; from one person of a country of concern engaged in a covered activity, or aggregated across such persons each contributing at least $50,000; based on the most recent audited (else unaudited, appraisal, good-faith estimate) statement (§ 850.209(b))
thresholds.consequence: A holder of a board seat, voting or equity interest or management power in such persons is a covered foreign person
thresholds.conditions: Alternative tests on net income, capital expenditure and operating expenses (§ 850.209(a)(2)(ii)-(iv)) use the same 50% cutoff

evidence.quote: Derives more than 50 percent of its revenue individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its revenue, on an annual basis

thresholds.measurement: As for revenue (§ 850.209(b))
thresholds.consequence: Holder is a covered foreign person

evidence.quote: Derives more than 50 percent of its net income individually

thresholds.value_text: more than 50 percent of its capital expenditure
thresholds.measurement: As for revenue (§ 850.209(b))
thresholds.consequence: Holder is a covered foreign person

evidence.quote: Incurs more than 50 percent of its capital expenditure individually

thresholds.value_text: more than 50 percent of its operating expenses
thresholds.measurement: As for revenue (§ 850.209(b))
thresholds.consequence: Holder is a covered foreign person

evidence.quote: Incurs more than 50 percent of its operating expenses individually

thresholds.variable_text: at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its revenue

thresholds.measurement: Annual amount derived from (or incurred with) each person of a country of concern engaged in a covered activity; non-USD amounts converted at Treasury's latest published rate (§ 850.209(b)(2)); applies equally to net income, capex and opex
thresholds.consequence: Only persons contributing at least this amount are aggregated toward the 50% tests

evidence.quote: as aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its revenue

thresholds.variable_text: voting interest, voting power of the board, or equity interest held by the government of a country of concern

thresholds.measurement: Held individually or in the aggregate, directly or indirectly; applied at two tiers ((d) by persons in (a)-(c); (e) by entities in (d))
thresholds.consequence: The entity is a person of a country of concern

evidence.quote: Any entity in which one or more persons identified in paragraph (a), (b), or (c) of this section, individually or in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, holds at least 50 percent of any of the following interests of such entity

thresholds.measurement: Direct or indirect holdings; in tiered structures subsidiary holdings are fully attributed and holdings of 50% or less are attributed proportionately (§ 850.206(b))

evidence.quote: The limited partner or equivalent's committed capital is not more than $2,000,000, aggregated across any investment and co-investment vehicles of the fund

obligations.summary: U.S. persons may not engage in a prohibited transaction unless a national interest exemption has been granted.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person may not engage in a prohibited transaction unless an exemption for that transaction has been granted under § 850.502.

obligations.summary: U.S. persons may not knowingly direct a non-U.S. person's transaction that would be prohibited for a U.S. person; officers or directors who recuse themselves from approval, document review and negotiation are not treated as directing it.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person is prohibited from knowingly directing a transaction by a non-U.S. person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the transaction would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.

obligations.summary: U.S. persons must take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent prohibited transactions by their controlled foreign entities; Treasury considers compliance agreements, governance rights, training, internal controls and testing or auditing.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person shall take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent any transaction by its controlled foreign entity that would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.

obligations.summary: U.S. persons must file an electronic notification of each notifiable transaction, with the information in § 850.405 and a certification, within 30 days of the completion date.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person that undertakes a notifiable transaction shall file a notification of that transaction with the Department of the Treasury pursuant to § 850.404.

obligations.summary: U.S. persons must notify Treasury of transactions by their controlled foreign entities that would be notifiable if engaged in by a U.S. person.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person shall file a notification with the Department of the Treasury pursuant to § 850.404 with respect to any transaction by a controlled foreign entity of that U.S. person that would be a notifiable transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.

obligations.summary: A U.S. person that learns after completion that a transaction would have been covered (notifiable or prohibited) must notify Treasury within 30 days, explaining why it lacked the knowledge and what diligence it did.
obligations.conditional_on: Actual knowledge acquired after the completion date

evidence.quote: This requirement applies regardless of whether the transaction would have been a notifiable transaction or a prohibited transaction.

obligations.summary: Notifications must contain the listed information (parties, ownership charts, rationale, transaction value, covered activities, end uses, technology nodes), accurate and complete in all material respects, or explain why information is unavailable and supply it within 30 days once available; pre-completion filings must be updated if materially changed.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person that has an obligation under this part to file a notification shall provide the information set forth in this section, which must be accurate and complete in all material respects

obligations.summary: Notifying U.S. persons must answer Treasury questions and document requests within the time and manner Treasury specifies; responses are part of the certified notification.

evidence.quote: The U.S. person shall respond to any such questions or requests within the time frame and in the manner specified by the Department of the Treasury.

obligations.summary: Notifying U.S. persons must keep the notification and supporting documentation (pitch decks, transaction documents, side letters, diligence materials) for ten years and provide them on request.

evidence.quote: Such supporting documentation shall include, as applicable, any pitch decks, marketing letters, and offering memorandums; transaction documents including side letters and investment agreements; and due diligence materials related to the transaction.

obligations.summary: Any person who made a representation, statement or certification under the part must tell Treasury in writing within 30 days of learning of a material omission or inaccuracy.

evidence.quote: A person who has made any representation, statement, or certification subject to this part shall inform the Department of the Treasury in writing promptly

obligations.summary: All filings must be in English; foreign-language supplementary materials are submitted in the original plus any existing English versions.

evidence.quote: All materials or information filed with the Department of the Treasury under this part shall be submitted in English.

obligations.summary: Any person must furnish under oath complete information on any act or transaction subject to the part when Treasury requires it, including exempted transactions; Treasury may investigate, hold hearings and subpoena witnesses and documents.

evidence.quote: Any person is required to furnish under oath, in the form of reports or otherwise, at any time as may be required by the Department of the Treasury, complete information regarding any act or transaction subject to the provisions of this part

obligations.summary: A U.S. person seeking a national interest exemption must submit information on the transaction, its analysis of the national-interest impact and a certification; exemptions are valid only in writing signed by the (Deputy) Assistant Secretary for Investment Security and may carry binding conditions.

evidence.quote: A U.S. person seeking a national interest exemption shall submit relevant information to the Department of the Treasury regarding the transaction and shall articulate the basis for the request

obligations.summary: A voluntary self-disclosure, considered in Treasury's response to a violation, must be a written notice describing the conduct and persons, followed by a sufficiently detailed report; disclosures prompted by agencies, subpoenas, third parties or required notifications do not qualify.
obligations.conditional_on: Person chooses to self-disclose possible violations

evidence.quote: A voluntary self-disclosure to the Department of the Treasury must take the form of a written notice describing the conduct that may constitute a violation and each of the persons involved.

obligations.summary: The Secretary of the Treasury shall, as appropriate, communicate with Congress and the public, consult Commerce, State, Defense, Energy and the DNI, engage allies, and investigate violations and pursue civil penalties.

evidence.quote: Investigate, in consultation with the heads of relevant agencies, as appropriate, violations of the Order or the regulations in this part and pursue available civil penalties for such violations.

obligations.summary: The Secretary shall periodically assess whether the AI training-compute criteria (10^23 notifiable; 10^25 and 10^24 prohibited) effectively address the threats and update them through public notice.

evidence.quote: shall periodically assess whether the criterion described in paragraph (k) of this section is serving to effectively address threats to the national security of the United States described in the Order and make updates, as appropriate, through public notice.

obligations.summary: Before designating third countries or transaction types for the § 850.501(g) exception the Secretary must consult State and Commerce, and designations, determinations and rescissions must be made public.

evidence.quote: Prior to making a designation or determination under this paragraph (g), the Secretary shall consult with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant agencies.

obligations.summary: Treasury must not publicly disclose non-public information submitted under the part, except in proceedings, to Congress, to domestic or allied governments, with consent, or when the Secretary (not below Assistant Secretary) finds disclosure in the national interest; anonymized data may be published.

evidence.quote: information or documentary materials not otherwise publicly available that are submitted to the Department of the Treasury under this part shall not be disclosed to the public

obligations.summary: Treasury publishes the inflation-adjusted maximum civil penalty annually, by 15 January, in the Federal Register and on the program website.

evidence.quote: Notice of the maximum penalty which may be assessed under this section will be published in the Federal Register

A machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments

The term covered transaction means a U.S. person's direct or indirect: (1) Acquisition of an equity interest or contingent equity interest in a person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the acquisition is a covered foreign person
A person of a country of concern that engages in a covered activity
any of the activities referred to in the definition of notifiable transaction in § 850.217 or prohibited transaction in § 850.224
The term notifiable transaction means a covered transaction (that is not a prohibited transaction) in which the relevant covered foreign person

The term prohibited transaction means a covered transaction in which the relevant covered foreign person or, with respect to a covered transaction described in § 850.210(a)(5), the relevant joint venture
The term excepted transaction means a transaction that meets the criteria in § 850.501.
The term country of concern has the meaning given to it in the Annex to the Order.

definitions.term: Person of a country of concern

evidence.quote: An entity with a principal place of business in, headquartered in, or incorporated in or otherwise organized under the laws of, a country of concern
The term U.S. person means any United States citizen, lawful permanent resident, entity organized under the laws of the United States
The term controlled foreign entity means any entity incorporated in, or otherwise organized under the laws of, a country other than the United States of which a U.S. person is a parent.
The general partner, managing member, or equivalent of the entity; or (c) The investment adviser to any entity that is a pooled investment fund
a financial interest (including debt) that currently does not constitute an equity interest but is convertible into, or provides the right to acquire, an equity interest
the earliest date upon which any interest, asset, property, or right is conveyed, assigned, delivered, or otherwise transferred to a U.S. person

Actual knowledge that a fact or circumstance exists or is substantially certain to occur; (b) An awareness of a high probability of a fact or circumstance's existence or future occurrence; or (c) Reason to know

a U.S. person “knowingly directs” a transaction when the U.S. person has authority, individually or as part of a group, to make or substantially participate in decisions on behalf of a non-U.S. person
the term develop means to engage in any stages prior to serial production, such as design or substantive modification
The term produce means to engage in any of the post-development stages of realizing the relevant technology or product
The term advanced packaging means to package integrated circuits in a manner that supports the two-and-one-half-dimensional (2.5D) or three-dimensional (3D) assembly of integrated circuits
The term fabricate means to form devices such as transistors, poly capacitors, non-metal resistors, and diodes on a wafer of semiconductor material.
The term package means to assemble various components, such as the integrated circuit die, lead frames, interconnects, and substrate materials
The term quantum computer means a computer that performs computations that harness the collective properties of quantum states, such as superposition, interference, or entanglement.

entities.note: General rule; no firms are named. Covered persons are identified by reference to the Annex to E.O. 14105 (countries of concern) and to lists kept elsewhere (BIS Entity List and MEU List, SDN and NS-CMIC Lists, FTO designations).

notes: Thresholds on prohibited vs notifiable activity are coded with trigger 'designation_category' (the rule sorts covered transactions into notifiable and prohibited tiers); the vocabulary has no 'prohibition' trigger. The 41,600 cubic-foot supercomputer envelope is a volume coded under floor_area for lack of a volume variable. The logic-node cutoff is written '16/14 nanometers or less' and coded as <= 16. The covered-foreign-person 50% tests (revenue, net income, capex, opex) are coded as four rows. Several criteria move with other instruments: ECCN 3A090.a, the BIS and Treasury lists, the countries of concern in the E.O. 14105 Annex, and the compute thresholds, which Treasury reassesses and updates by public notice. Countries of concern are named only in the preamble (PRC, Hong Kong, Macau, citing the Annex). Civil penalties: the current inflation-adjusted figure is published annually.
